title: Renewing Network Observability for the AI Era
summary: Check out the latest IDC Link report covering NETSCOUT's ENGAGE 2026 conference. Dive into how to renew network observability for the AI era with IDC and NETSCOUT experts.
body_markdown:
What will it take to turn AI’s promise into trusted operational reality? As organizations move beyond AI experimentation, agents, copilots, and automation increasingly influence operational decisions. That leaves a concerning challenge: AI is only as reliable as the data and context informing its decisions.


Traditional observability approaches provide valuable telemetry but can lack a complete and trusted operational picture that AI-driven operations require. In the new IDC Link report “[NETSCOUT ENGAGE 2026: Renewing Network Observability for the AI Era](https://www.netscout.com/resources/reports/netscout-engage-2026-renewing-network-observability-for-the-ai-era) ,” IDC assesses how the network observability market is evolving and how NETSCOUT is positioning itself to address the shifts.


## The Role of Network-Derived, Contextualized Data


Network-derived intelligence is central to the evolution of observability. As AI takes on a greater role in IT operations, the question is not just what networks can tell us. Instead, it is about what the network can tell us and the context those insights can provide to companies.


IDC explores[NETSCOUT’s AI-ready Smart Data Platform](https://www.netscout.com/platform) and its approach to bringing network intelligence to AI-driven workflows. For IT professionals, IDC’s perspective offers thoughtful insights into the way NETSCOUT’s solutions fulfill these objectives.


The innovations across[NETSCOUT’s observability portfolio](https://www.netscout.com/observability) reflect a broader shift toward AI-ready operations. The implications extend beyond visibility and troubleshooting to faster operational understanding, more evidence-based decisions, and the move toward more predictive and preventive network management.


NETSCOUT’s commitment to technology innovation and leadership continues with three recent product-related announcements designed to help enterprise organizations benefit from the full potential of AI-powered network operations. These innovations include NETSCOUT’s AI-ready Smart Data Platform, featuring Omnis AI Insights with[Omnis Sensor](https://www.netscout.com/product/omnis-sensor) and[Omnis Streamer](https://www.netscout.com/product/omnis-streamer) ; Model Context Protocol (MCP) connectivity that makes[Smart Data](https://www.netscout.com/what-is/smart-data) accessible to AI assistants and agents; and[nGenius Copilot](https://www.netscout.com/product/ngenius-copilot) , which brings conversational AI to the[nGeniusONE network observability solution](https://www.netscout.com/product/ngeniusone-solution) .


Trust and confidence will be a defining consideration as observability architectures evolve. Enterprises will need to evaluate the data behind AI-driven operations and distinguish the veracity of reliable operational context from incomplete or inferred telemetry. Observability architectures that depend on network ground truth, such as Smart Data, are the best fit for the next generation of AI-driven workflows.


IDC offers an independent perspective on the challenges and opportunities highlighted here and how NETSCOUT’s technology and strategy addresses them. **Discover more in the IDC Link report “**[NETSCOUT ENGAGE 2026: Renewing Network Observability for the AI Era, ”](https://www.netscout.com/resources/reports/netscout-engage-2026-renewing-network-observability-for-the-ai-era) **which focuses on NETSCOUT’s latest innovations, differentiations, and trust implications on enterprise AI operations.**
